question: Why the single-RAW estimator overestimates the shot slope at ISO 100 on daylight photos (60D x1.6 median), and whether a bound is needed.
photos: ordinary CR2 (EOS 60D, qualified law) and CR3 (EOS R6 Mark III, catalogue law) of tests/image, at most 12 per ISO, outside the protocol and burst folders

fixed_pattern_on_60d_flats.method: per 64-pixel tile of the G plane, plane removed: temporal variance from the pair difference over 1 + k^2, fixed variance = variance of the pair mean minus half the temporal; median over tiles

visual_check: IMG_6222 (slope x2.6-3.5) and IMG_6954 (x1.4-1.5), 256 x 256 per plane, input / qualified / estimated law: no visible difference at ISO 100 (user review pending)
